oliver: Heads-up — we just saw a 3x jump in 99th latency for /generate on dedicated-prod (g4x pool) during the 18:12 burst. Throughput dropped ~40%.

oliver: Quick numbers: p99 went 85ms -> 260ms, p50 steady. Warm pool count shows no new warmed instances for ~90s while scale-up requests were in-flight.

maya: Ugh. Can you paste the runtime profiler and autoscaler logs?

oliver: Paste below. profiler snapshot shows repeated kernel fallback and recompile hits for layer matmul. KV cache miss rate spiked too.

oliver: ```
[profiler] seq_len=1024 tasks=48
kernel_selector: chose optimized_matmul_v2 for shapes (1024,1024) 
kernel_selector: fallback to generic_matmul (recompile) x3, compile_time=1.9s
kv-cache: miss_rate=0.72, eviction_rate=0.18
serving: new-instance-requested id=pool-req-22 status=pending
serving: warm-pool-count=2 target=6
```

autoscaler-bot: Received scale request pool=g4x target=+4 at 1765678845, provisioning started. Provisioner: queued because host allocator getting backoff from noisy-neighbor mitigation. Estimated ready ETA=70s.

oliver: The timeline shows the autoscaler requested new GPUs but the runtime spent ~5s per request recompiling kernels on first requests, so warmups didn't finish before traffic spiked.

james: Was there a recent change to kernel selection heuristics? That recompile pattern looks like a heuristic flip causing layout-transform kernels to be preferred, then fallback.

deploy-bot: Deployed: kernel-heuristics v2.1 -> v2.2 at 1765674000 (canary to prod).

maya: yep that rollout matches. v2.2 introduced dynamic-layout preference based on sequence distribution. I asked for a slow ramp but looks like canary wasn't restrictive enough.

sophie: Also KV cache miss spike implies prefix cache invalidation / eviction. If warm instances get recompiled and restart caching layer they lose hot KVs -> miss cascade.

perfbot: Profile diff between 1765673000 and 1765678800 shows average kernel init time +1.6s, cache hits -0.42, p99 +175ms for affected models.

james: Repro steps that helped me locally: use the workload runner with these args 
```
./workload-runner --model rdx-base-1 --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 48 --warmup 0
```
It forces first-hot requests and exposes the compile/regress.

oliver: Mitigation proposed: 1) rollback kernel-heuristics to v2.1 (fast), 2) temporarily bump warm-pool target by +3 for g4x while we validate, 3) add stricter canary constraints before global rollout.

sophie: Agreed. Also add a short KV-preserve flag on instance bootstrap to avoid cache eviction while we scale.

maya: I'll trigger rollback and increase warm pool. Oncall, please prioritize provisioning backlog.

oncall: Acknowledged, clearing queue and prioritizing warm pool.

deploy-bot: Rolling back kernel-heuristics to v2.1 (initiated) at 1765679025.

autoscaler-bot: Warm pool target updated: g4x target +=3 at 1765679050. Provisioning ETA updated -> 25s.

oliver: After rollback + warm pool bump, p99 is back to ~95ms in the last 60s window. Throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline.

maya: Closing immediate incident. Action items: (a) revert release process for heuristics until more canary signals added, (b) add kernel-init time metric and alert, (c) KV-preserve bootstrap experiment, (d) add test to throughput-ageing in perf suite.

james: I'll put PRs for canary gating and kernel-init metric.

sophie: I'll own the KV-preserve experiment and a test for cache warm continuity.

oliver: Filing postmortem doc with timelines and graphs after this thread. Thanks. :thumbsup:

maya: Good job triaging. We'll review the perf diffs in Monday's runtime sync. :eyes:
